title: Notary, Power of Attorney & Sworn Translators in Türkiye
seoTitle: Power of Attorney in Türkiye: Notary & Sworn Translators
metaDescription: How to issue a limited Power of Attorney in Türkiye safely in 2026: notary fees, sworn translator rules, risky clauses to avoid, and consulate steps.
quickAnswer: Foreign nationals can issue a limited Power of Attorney (vekaletname) in Türkiye at any licensed notary office (noter) with a passport, Turkish tax number, and sworn translator, or abroad via a Turkish consulate or Hague Apostille. Restrict every property POA to specific parcels, forbid selling or mortgaging, and verify your attorney first.

body.text: How do you issue a limited Power of Attorney (Vekaletname) safely in Türkiye or at a consulate?

Issuing a power of attorney turkey document safely starts with a narrow, task-specific draft reviewed by an independent Turkish lawyer before you enter a notary office. In Türkiye, you sign in person before a notary with a sworn interpreter; abroad, you sign at a Turkish consulate or use a local notary plus an Apostille.

Inside Türkiye, any notary listed via the [Union of Turkish Notaries (TNB)](https://portal.tnb.org.tr/Sayfalar/Noterbul.aspx) executes a vekaletname the same day. Bring your passport, notarized Turkish passport translation, Turkish tax number, and two biometric photos for real estate deeds.
Abroad, choose between two compliant routes:

items: Turkish Consulate: Book an in-person appointment via the [Ministry of Foreign Affairs e-Konsolosluk portal](https://www.konsolosluk.gov.tr/Procedure/ShowProcedure/6). The consulate drafts the POA directly in Turkish for immediate use once couriered to Türkiye.
Local Notary + Apostille: Sign before a local notary, obtain a Hague Apostille, and courier the original to Türkiye for sworn translation and Turkish notarization.
Verify Your Lawyer: Confirm active bar registration on the [Union of Turkish Bar Associations (TBB) Lawyer Search](https://barobirlik.org.tr/AvukatArama) before naming any representative.
Set an Expiry Date: Insert a fixed 6-to-12-month validity window.

body.text: Why must a sworn translator be present at every notary and TAPU signing?

Turkish law mandates a licensed sworn translator (yeminli tercüman) at every notary execution and Land Registry (TAPU) transfer whenever a foreign signatory is not fluent in Turkish. The interpreter translates the full deed aloud before you sign and co-signs the record to confirm informed consent under the [General Directorate of Land Registry and Cadastre (TKGM)](https://www.tkgm.gov.tr/yabanci-isler-dairesi-baskanligi/forforeigners).

Without an accredited interpreter sworn in at that notary office, the notary cannot legally authenticate a foreign signature on a vekaletname or sales contract. Distinguish between two translation levels: a sworn translation (yeminli tercüme) carries the translator's stamp, whereas a notarized translation (noter onaylı tercüme) adds notary certification required for passports, foreign POAs, and registry files.
What powers should you NEVER grant blindly in a property POA?

Never sign a general Power of Attorney (genel vekaletname) for a property purchase or grant authority to a real estate agent or developer employee. A safe property POA names only an independent licensed attorney and restricts authority to purchasing a specified parcel, registering utilities, and collecting the title deed.
Standard notary templates include broad boilerplate unless you remove these clauses:

items: Power to sell (satış yetkisi): A buying POA must never include resale rights.
Power to mortgage (ipotek tesis etme): Forbid placing liens or loans on your title deed.
Bank withdrawal rights: Execute purchase transfers yourself rather than granting cash withdrawal access.
Unlimited sub-delegation (tevkil): Limit delegation strictly to named partners within the same law firm.

body.text: How much do notary and sworn translation fees cost?

Under the [2026 Turkish Notary Fee Tariff](https://portal.tnb.org.tr/Tebligler/Noterlik%20%C3%9Ccret%20Tarifesi.pdf) effective 1 January 2026, notary fees are regulated nationwide by page count, copies, and statutory ratios. A limited property POA executed in Türkiye—including notary charges, sworn translation, and live interpreter attendance—typically totals TRY 4,500 to TRY 9,500 depending on page length.

faq.q: Can I revoke a Turkish Power of Attorney after issuing it?
faq.a: Yes. Sign a formal deed of revocation (azilname) at any Turkish notary or consulate and notify your former representative and the Land Registry office immediately.

faq.q: Does a Power of Attorney issued abroad need an Apostille?
faq.a: POAs signed at a Turkish consulate need no Apostille. POAs signed before a local foreign notary require a Hague Apostille (or diplomatic legalization) plus notarized Turkish translation.

faq.q: Can my spouse or friend act as my translator at a Turkish notary?
faq.a: No. Turkish notaries accept only accredited sworn translators registered with that notary office.

faq.q: Do I need a Turkish tax number before issuing a property POA?
faq.a: Yes. Obtain a free Turkish tax number (vergi kimlik numarası) beforehand so the notary and Land Registry can tie the authorization to your identity.

faq.q: How long does a limited Power of Attorney remain valid in Türkiye?
faq.a: Unless an expiration date is written into the deed, a Turkish POA stays valid until revoked. Adding a 6-to-12-month expiry clause is standard practice.

faq.q: Can a POA cover utility connections after I buy a home?
faq.a: Yes. You can authorize electricity, water, natural gas, internet, and municipal tax registration without granting selling or borrowing powers.
